chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Bashir ibn Ja'far from Abu Usamah al-Hannat said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A relative of mine or a man by marriage of mine swore that if his wife exits the door, she is divorced three times.' So she exited, and her husband had intercourse with her as God willed from the hardship. He ordered me to ask you, so he leaned towards me and said: 'Order him to keep her; it is not [considered] anything [i.e., the third divorce does not take effect].' Then he turned to the people and said: 'Glory be to God, they order her to marry [another man] while she still has a husband.'

key_terms.المَشَقّة: Hardship / difficulty (referring to the period of waiting or consummation)
key_terms.صِهْر: Man by marriage / relative by marriage
key_terms.لَيْسَ بشَيْءٍ: It is not [considered] anything (i.e., not effective as a third divorce)

ai.seo_question: Does a triple divorce pronounced in one sitting count as three separate divorces or just one in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that a triple divorce pronounced in a single sitting counts as only one effective divorce, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence from the Sunni view of 'triple talaq'. The Imam clarified that since the wife had already consummated the marriage after the pronouncement but before final separation, the husband was ordered to keep her, meaning the third divorce did not sever the marriage permanently. This ruling emphasizes that the 'waiting period' (Iddah) begins upon the first pronouncement, and subsequent pronouncements in the same context do not immediately dissolve the bond if intimacy has occurred.
